text:
alex: quick sync — ran the production-trace replay (anonymized slice) on kernel-selector v2 + batch-adapt=true. baseline is kernel-selector v1 with batch-adapt=false. saw ~18% increase in p95 latency and a small drop in throughput on the 80k-user slice. attaching quick notes below.

maria: ouch. which model + quantization? kv hit rates?

alex: llama-70b-unq (no quant) for this run to avoid quant noise. KV hit rate dropped from 0.83 -> 0.71 on the failing cohort. token/sec fell ~12%.

devin: can you paste the exact run command + sample selection parameters? want to repro locally.

alex: sure — this is the harness command:
```
./replay_harness --trace /mnt/traces/prod_slice_2026_02_11.jsonl \ 
  --kernel-selector v2 --batch-adapt auto --kv-prefetch on \ 
  --anonymize-policy scrub-ttl --cohort-sampling stratified=1000 \ 
  --out /tmp/replay-run-2823456789.log
```

sam: two quick checks: 1) deterministic seeds? 2) were any fallback kernels triggered during the run? fallback can change perf characteristics.

alex: seed=42 set in the harness. fallback events present but infrequent — ~3% of requests fell back to cpu-fallback path because the chosen kernel wasn't available on that GPU. I filtered those out in the baseline vs candidate comparison.

maria: the KV hit rate delta is worrying. did the replay respect the same prefix caching window and TTLs as prod? sometimes anonymization scrubs prefixes and kills cache hits.

alex: good call. anonymize-policy=scrub-ttl removes user identifiers but preserves normalized prefixes. I'll re-run with scrub-preserve-prefix to confirm.

devin: for apples-to-apples: we should run three experiments:
- A: baseline (v1, batch-adapt=false)
- B: v2 but batch-adapt=false (kernel change only)
- C: v2 + batch-adapt=true (both changes)
This will isolate kernel selector vs batching heuristic impact.

bench-bot: queued jobs: run-A(2823457001), run-B(2823457102), run-C(2823457203). ETA ~45m. will post aggregated metrics when ready. :gear:

alex: thanks. also want a deterministic log-level diff check for logits to detect functional drift: compare token-prob deltas and token-stream divergence counts. if >0.001 L2 on logits for >0.5% of tokens we flag as non-parity.

sam: how are you computing token-prob deltas? floating noise will creep in with different kernels. need epsilon tolerance and normalized sequence alignment.

alex: using stable sort of token ids + aligner that tolerates sub-token splits. metric script: `scripts/logit_compare.py --baseline baseline.log --candidate candidate.log --tolerance 1e-3 --report /tmp/logit-diff.json`

maria: when bench-bot posts numbers, please include KV hit rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and kernel-switch counts. Also include the sample id distribution so we can check cohort skew.

ops-bot: small FYI — upcoming infra maintenance in eu-west-1 at 03:00 UTC may affect any runs hitting that region.

devin: if we see parity for B but regression in C then blame is batch-adapt heuristics; if B regresses too, it's kernel selector. good plan.

bench-bot: run-A done: p95=142ms, p50=24ms, tokens/sec=1.9M, kv_hit=0.83, kernel-switches=0.  run-B done: p95=154ms, p50=25ms, tokens/sec=1.82M, kv_hit=0.82, kernel-switches=0->v2=0. run-C partial: p95=168ms, p50=27ms, tokens/sec=1.67M, kv_hit=0.71, kernel-switches=0->v2 with batch-adapt toggles=12% of requests. full C will finish in ~6m.

alex: interesting — B shows small hit but C much worse. suggests batching heuristic + KV interactions. maybe batch-adapt is increasing batch sizes and evicting KV entries sooner (memory pressure).

sam: can we get a memory occupancy trace across the run? both GPU mem and KV cache size. if batch sizes jump, KV cache may be evicted under our current allocator.

bench-bot: attached sample memory timeline (short log excerpt):
```
[00:01:12] gpu_mem_used=12.4G kv_cache_entries=1.2M
[00:13:08] gpu_mem_used=19.1G kv_cache_entries=0.82M  # spike correlated with batch-adapt increase
[00:13:11] fallback_cpu=0.03%
```

maria: that matches KV hit drop. batch-adapt likely increased per-device batch occupancy causing more KV churn. can we cap batch-adapt max_batch_size and re-run C?

devin: propose a followup: C1 = v2 + batch-adapt=true + max_batch=64, C2 = v2 + batch-adapt=true + kv-prefetch=aggressive. both runs will isolate whether it's batch sizing or kv prefetch policy.

alex: agreed. also let's instrument latency per-token-after-kv-hit vs token-after-kv-miss to quantify impact. add `--emit-kv-metrics` flag.

bench-bot: queued C1(2823457404) and C2(2823457505). will publish diff table when done.

alex: one more note on determinism: even with seed=42 we saw tiny non-deterministic kernel fallback ordering in v2 that causes rare logit diffs. for parity checks we'll mask sequences where fallback_count>0.

maria: perfect. thanks all — once C1/C2 finish let's reconvene and decide whether to roll back batch-adapt default or tune allocator thresholds. :+1:

devin: if we decide to tune, let's do canary rollout to 5% and monitor p95 & kv_hit in real-time.

alex: will collect artifacts and open a short PR with the run configs and logs at <https://redwood.internal/runs/2823456789>.
